Use case: style-transfer. Asset: 2x2 pixel-art skeleton enemy combat sprite sheet, production art for a 4x NES tactical RPG remake.
Input 1 is the EXACT four native pose/part/order reference. Input 2 is ONLY the subdued blue-purple palette and matte pixel-art rendering style reference; do NOT turn the skeleton into that human character.
Redraw all FOUR complete skeletal guards from Input 1 as the SAME bone guard, in a strict 2 columns x 2 rows order. Top left native pose0 standing with close feet; top right pose1 first bent-knee running phase; bottom left pose2 wide stride and back arm extended behind; bottom right pose3 passing phase with both knees near the center. MATCH each native pose and which upper/lower arm and leg is in front or behind. Preserve the skull facing left, clear empty eye socket, real jaw/teeth, rib cage, spine, exposed bony pelvis, thin connected bones, bony fingers and skeletal feet. All are skeletons with no skin or flesh. Same bone lengths and same scale, no missing bones, no extra limbs. The knees/feet must follow the corresponding source phase, not a generic walking stance.
Battle equipment: ONE plain moderately curved single-edge sword held by the foreground hand at screen-left, blade rising forward/up-left from its hilt, exactly like the source. The rear hand/arm at screen-right is EMPTY and bent back; there is NO shield in these native battle sprites. Interpret the purple parts in the native as restrained worn blue-purple wrist/ankle bindings. No chestplate hiding the ribs, no big armor, no helmet, no hair, no cape, no new garments hiding the pelvis or legs. No magic/aura/glowing eyes.
Palette: soft and readable, NOT dark gray. Pale warm ivory bone (#d9d8c5), muted lavender bone shadows (#9b9eb4), deep navy outlines (#172638), subdued blue-purple wraps (#57577f) with navy-purple shade (#343c5d), muted cold steel blade (#bac4d2), occasional dusty-purple hilt (#8f7b8d). About 7 flat material colors, no gradients, no dithering/noise, no specular highlights on wraps or bones. Necessary dark eye cavities, joint and rib separations remain visible.
Clean handmade pixel art, the same chunky small-pixel finish as Input2, not painting, not vector icons. Four separate complete figures, plenty of transparent gutters. All feet and sword tips included. Same standing ground baseline within each cell, stable skull/body center between these four running poses except the tiny native crouch in pose2. Enlarge each native sprite uniformly for legibility, retaining its silhouette proportions and exact hand/foot positions relative to its own torso. Absolutely no labels/text, no checkerboard, no backgrounds or shadows; genuinely transparent alpha. Do not include motion trails in these four poses.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Redraw the EXACT 4 native combat poses in input1 as the skeletal guard in input2. Strict 2x2 layout, all characters same physical scale. The subject is the SAME bare skeletal guard as reference2: ivory skull and exposed ribs/spine/pelvis, thin connected bone arms and legs, matte subdued blue-purple wrist and shin bindings, dark navy outlines, pale ivory bones with muted lavender shadows, plain cool-steel moderately curved sword and dusty-purple hilt. No flesh/skin, no hair, no helmet, no chestplate, no cape, no glowing eyes. Keep natural skeletal joints, two arms, two legs, bony fingers and feet. Distinguish the source's open lower jaw (small curved bone at the front of the neck, connected to the skull hinge) from arms; never add a third arm. About 7 flat material colors: #172638 #d9d8c5 #9b9eb4 #57577f #343c5d #bac4d2 #8f7b8d. Soft low saturation but light and readable, not gray/gloomy. Necessary shadows and outlines; no shiny bones/wrap highlights, no gradients/dithering/noise. Clean chunky 4x tactical-RPG pixel art, not painting or 3D. All parts complete, transparent gutters, NO background/ground/shadow/glow/text/checkerboard, genuine transparent alpha.
Input1 pose order: top-left native4, top-right native5, bottom-left native7, bottom-right native8. Each source body is a full skeletal figure; some thin bones appear isolated at tiny NES resolution, reconnect them anatomically while preserving their positions.
Top-left4: low wide-legged preparation, sword hand extends low toward screen-left, sword held low almost horizontal, empty rear arm bent behind the right shoulder.
Top-right5: wide-legged wind-up, sword hand drawn far behind screen-right with curved sword rising up-right; empty other arm extends up-left. THIS IS A TURN OF THE WHOLE UPPER BODY; do not keep the sword in front or invent an extra sword.
Bottom-left7: original rapid swing transition, sword arm fully raised overhead/up-left, extended bony arm connects shoulder to the hand above the skull; a SINGLE thin pale-lavender C-shaped blade sweep lies far to the LEFT of the body, matching the source7 arc. This sweep is only motion effect, not another arm or weapon. Skeleton legs stay in their original wide lunge.
Bottom-right8: same final overhead sword-arm posture and wide lunge as source8, NO C-shaped sweep. The original sword is ABOVE the overhead hand; the long vertical purple piece beneath the hand is its wrist/forearm wrapping, not a longer blade. Preserve blade length from the standing design in input2, don't stretch the sword. Skull and rib cage stay below this extended arm.
Match each reference's limbs, front/behind layering and silhouette, source hand and foot positions. All skeletal feet stay complete; retain the original foreground/back leg and arm. No shield in these combat poses. Do not change the poses into generic sword slashes. Make room above the lower two figures for the extended arm and sword without shrinking the character body scale.

STRICT layout: top-left BACK UP phase0 (source slot0), top-middle RIGHT-facing phase0 (slot2), top-right FRONT DOWN phase0 (slot4); bottom-left BACK UP phase1 (slot1), bottom-middle RIGHT phase1 (slot3), bottom-right FRONT DOWN phase1 (slot5). Columns are directions; rows are the two gait phases.
Native MAP equipment: small upright sword plus ROUND shield, not the bare rear hand in combat identity. UP/back column: sword in screen-RIGHT hand, shield in screen-LEFT hand, rear skull has NO eyes or facial features; show spine/scapulae and back of bony pelvis, no front chest. RIGHT side column: sword at screen-RIGHT in forward hand, shield behind torso on screen-LEFT seen from side, profile skull faces RIGHT. FRONT/down column: sword in screen-LEFT hand, shield in screen-RIGHT hand, frontal skull has two empty eye sockets and attached compact jaw.
Legs/arms: copy BOTH source gait phases precisely, including which leg is in FRONT/BACK, which knee is lifted and which foot contacts the ground. UP phase0 has screen-right foot planted, screen-left leg bent/lifted; UP phase1 reverses. DOWN phase0 has screen-left foot planted and screen-right foot lifted, DOWN phase1 reverses. RIGHT phase0 is a wide stride with legs clearly separated in depth; RIGHT phase1 is the passing step with one foot crossing behind the other. Use source body silhouettes for limb positions and keep visible bony gaps; don't replace phases by identical legs or swap front/back limbs. Behind-thigh/behind-forearm must be occluded correctly by the front bone, pelvis or shield.
Each direction's skull, spine/ribcage center and pelvis must remain at exactly the SAME coordinates across the top/bottom pair. No whole-sprite horizontal/vertical shift or bob. Only legs and arms articulate as in source. The sword and shield follow their hand without stretching, detached fingers or jumping. Same body scale across all 6 figures, enough transparent gutters. Small map skulls/connected jaws, no large open floating jaws. No effects or extra action.

Use case: style-transfer. Two full pixel-art combat sprites for the SAME skeletal bone guard, strict 2 columns x 1 row, transparent background. Image1 is the EXACT ORIGINAL POSE guide; Image2 is the established character appearance only. Native anatomical proportions in Image1: ground y64, skull center around (43,36), raised hand around (32,20), sword tip around (39,5). Thus the hand is about HALF a bare-body height ABOVE the skull center, significantly LEFT of the skull; the complete figure from swordtip to feet is almost TWICE the skull-to-feet body height. Show a continuous bony upper arm from shoulder diagonally up-left to high elbow, then an extended wrapped forearm to the high hand. Sword is the same moderately curved blade length as Image2, above that hand. Keep skull/torso/leg sizes consistent with Image2 and do not shrink the lower body to fit. Soft low saturation, light readable bones, no gloom, no surface highlights, gradients or dithering. Clean coarse pixel-art. No backgrounds, glow/halo, labels or shadows. Genuine transparent alpha.
